paragraphs: Rabbi Menachem, brother of Rabbi Gurion.

Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 9:8 has him explaining a teaching before Rabbi La (whom Hyman identifies as Rabbi Ila). Seder HaDorot misread this as “before Rabbi,” attaching la, “not,” to the next word: “not better to sow it with flax.” The proper division is “before Rabbi La: it is better to sow it,” etc. Rabbi La appears frequently in the Jerusalem Talmud; the name abbreviates Elai, as explained in that entry.

notes.text: The negation-versus-name argument depends on punctuation: La is the sage addressed, not “not” attached to “better.” Ila and Elai are Hyman’s own name forms and explanation.

The consulted Guggenheimer Bava Metzia 9:8 explicitly reads Rabbi Menachem, brother of Rabbi Gurion, before Rabbi La, followed by “better to sow.” This supports the name/negation division. Hyman’s criticism of Seder HaDorot and Ila/Elai explanation remain his claims.
